units.zh: 少苦心為學，以明經調補華州參軍，拔萃登科，授鄠縣尉。
units.en: In his youth he applied himself rigorously to learning. He passed the classics examination and was appointed aide in Huazhou. After winning selection in the superior examination he was made assistant magistrate of E County.
units.literal: In youth he painstakingly studied; through the classics examination he was appointed Huazhou aide; selected in the superior examination and passed; granted Assistant Magistrate of E County.

units.zh: 周歷臺省，由左司郎中出為常州刺史。
units.en: He served in various posts in the Secretariat and Chancellery, and left the capital from his post as Director in the Left Bureau to become prefect of Changzhou.
units.literal: He passed through the Secretariat and Chancellery offices; from Director in the Left Bureau he went out as Prefect of Changzhou.

units.zh: 逾年，召為給事中，出為湖南觀察使，銳於為理。
units.en: A year later he was recalled to serve as a Supervising Secretariat Drafter, then sent out as commissioner of Hunan, where he governed with sharp efficiency.
units.literal: After a year he was summoned as Supervising Secretary, sent out as Hunan Observation Commissioner; he was keen on governance.

units.zh: 五年，改江西觀察使，加檢校散騎常侍、兼御史大夫。
units.en: In his fifth year he was transferred to Jiangxi as observation commissioner, with the additional titles of Acting Regular Palace Attendant and Concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: In the fifth year he was changed to Jiangxi Observation Commissioner, with additional Acting Regular Palace Attendant and concurrent Censor-in-Chief.

units.zh: 巽持下以法，吏不敢欺，而動必察之。
units.en: Li Xun governed his subordinates strictly by law. Clerks did not dare cheat him—and he scrutinized every move they made.
units.literal: Xun held subordinates by law; clerks did not dare deceive, yet every movement he surely investigated.

units.zh: 順宗即位，入為兵部侍郎。
units.en: When Emperor Shunzong came to the throne, Li Xun was brought back to serve as Vice Minister of Military Affairs.
units.literal: When Shunzong took the throne, he entered the capital as Vice Minister of Military Affairs.

units.zh: 司徒杜佑判度支鹽鐵轉運使，以巽幹治，奏為副使。
units.en: Situ Du You headed the finance, salt, iron, and transport commission. Impressed by Li Xun's administrative skill, he recommended him as deputy commissioner.
units.literal: Situ Du You presided over finance, salt, iron, and transport; because Xun was capable in administration, he memorialized him as vice commissioner.

units.zh: 佑辭重位，巽遂專領度支鹽鐵使。
units.en: When Du You stepped down from the heavy office, Li Xun took sole charge of the finance and salt commission.
units.literal: You declined the heavy post; Xun then solely headed the Finance and Salt Commissioner.

units.zh: 榷筦之法，號為難重，唯大歷中僕射劉晏雅得其術，賦入豐羨。
units.en: The state monopoly system was notoriously difficult to manage. Only in the Dali era had Vice Director Liu Yan truly mastered it, yielding abundant revenue.
units.literal: The monopoly-and-control laws were called difficult and heavy; only in the Dali era Vice Director Liu Yan elegantly mastered their technique, and tax revenue was abundant.

units.zh: 巽掌使一年，征課所入，類晏之多歲，明年過之，又一年加一百八十萬貫。
units.en: In his first year in office Li Xun's tax collections matched Liu Yan's best years. The next year he exceeded that total, and in the following year he added another 1.8 million strings of cash.
units.literal: Xun held the commission one year; revenue collected matched Yan's many plentiful years; the next year surpassed it; in another year he added one million eight hundred thousand strings.

units.zh: 舊制，每歲運江淮米五十萬斛抵河陰，久不盈其數，唯巽三年登焉。
units.en: By regulation five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai grain were shipped each year to Heyin, a quota long unmet—until Li Xun fulfilled it three years running.
units.literal: By old regulation, each year five hundred thousand shi of Jiang-Huai rice were transported to Heyin; for a long time the quota was not filled; only Xun in three years achieved it.

units.zh: 遷兵部尚書，明年改吏部尚書，使任如故。
units.en: He was promoted to Minister of Military Affairs, and the following year transferred to Minister of Personnel while retaining his commission unchanged.
units.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Military Affairs; the next year changed to Minister of Personnel; his commissioner duties remained as before.

units.zh: 巽精於吏職，蓋性使然也。
units.en: Li Xun excelled at bureaucratic work—it was simply in his nature.
units.literal: Xun was expert in administrative duties—probably his nature was such.

units.zh: 雖在私家，亦置案牘簿書，勾檢如公署焉。
units.en: Even at home he kept files and ledgers, auditing accounts as though he were still in a government office.
units.literal: Even in private life he also set out dossiers and ledgers, checking accounts like a public office.

units.zh: 人吏有過，絲毫無所貸，雖在千里外，其恐栗如在巽前。
units.en: He showed subordinates no mercy whatever for any fault. Even a thousand li away they trembled as though he were standing over them.
units.literal: When men and clerks had faults, not the slightest was forgiven; even a thousand li away, they trembled in fear as if before Xun.

units.zh: 初，程異附王叔文貶竄，巽知其吏才明辯，奏而用之，憲宗不違其請。
units.en: Cheng Yi had earlier been exiled for siding with Wang Shuwen, but Li Xun recognized his talent for clear, forceful administration and recommended him for office. Emperor Xianzong granted the request.
units.literal: At first Cheng Yi, having attached himself to Wang Shuwen, was exiled; Xun knew his clerical talent was clear and eloquent, memorialized and used him; Xianzong did not refuse his request.

units.zh: 異勾檢簿籍，又精於巽，故課最加衍，亦異之助焉。
units.en: Cheng Yi audited the books with even greater skill than Li Xun himself, so revenue totals kept climbing—with Cheng Yi's help.
units.literal: Yi checked ledgers and account books, and was even more expert than Xun; therefore assessment yields increased and expanded—also Yi's assistance.

units.zh: 巽為吏部尚書，臥疾，郎官相率省問，巽初不言其病，與之考校程課，商略功利，至其夕而卒。
units.en: While serving as Minister of Personnel, Li Xun fell ill. When bureau directors came in succession to visit, he at first said nothing of his illness and instead reviewed schedules and quotas with them, discussing business until he died that evening.
units.literal: Xun was Minister of Personnel, ill abed; bureau directors successively came to inquire; Xun at first did not speak of his illness, and with them examined schedules and quotas, discussed profit and utility—by that evening he died.

units.zh: 然性強很狡惡，忌刻頗甚，乘德宗之怒，謀殺竇參，物論冤之。
units.en: Yet he was by nature stubborn, ruthless, and deeply jealous. Exploiting Emperor Dezong's wrath he engineered the death of Dou Can—a killing widely regarded as unjust.
units.literal: Yet his nature was obstinate, cunning, and wicked; his jealousy and harshness were quite severe; riding Dezong's anger, he plotted to kill Dou Can—public opinion deemed it a wrongful death.

units.zh: 初，參為宰相，不悅於巽，自左司郎中出為常州刺史，仍促其行。
units.en: Earlier, when Dou Can was chancellor, Li Xun had fallen out of his favor. Can had him transferred from Director in the Left Bureau to prefect of Changzhou and pressed him to leave at once.
units.literal: At first when Can was chancellor, displeased with Xun, from Director in the Left Bureau he was sent out as Prefect of Changzhou, and his departure was still hurried.

units.zh: 不數月，參貶郴州司馬。
units.en: Within months Dou Can himself was demoted to military aide at Chenzhou.
units.literal: Within not many months Can was demoted to Military Aide of Chenzhou.

units.zh: 久之，巽自給事中為湖南觀察使，郴即屬郡也。
units.en: Later, after Li Xun had risen from Supervising Secretariat Drafter to Hunan observation commissioner, Chenzhou fell under his jurisdiction.
units.literal: After a long time, Xun went from Supervising Secretary to Hunan Observation Commissioner—Chenzhou was precisely a subordinate prefecture.

units.zh: 宣武軍節度使劉士寧以擅襲父任，物議不可，朝廷不得已而授之。
units.en: Liu Shining of Xuanwu Circuit had seized his father's command without authorization—a move widely condemned, yet the court had no choice but to confirm the appointment.
units.literal: Xuanwu Circuit Military Governor Liu Shining, for seizing his father's post on his own authority, was unacceptable in public opinion; the court had no choice but to appoint him.

units.zh: 及參之貶，士寧嘗以絹數千匹賂參，巽在湖南具奏其事，言參與籓鎮交通，德宗怒，遂賜參死，議者冤之。
units.en: When Dou Can was demoted, Liu Shining had once given him several thousand bolts of silk as a bribe. Reporting from Hunan, Li Xun laid out the full story, accusing Can of trafficking with frontier military governors. Emperor Dezong was enraged and ordered Dou Can executed—a death many considered a miscarriage of justice.
units.literal: When Can was demoted, Shining had once bribed Can with several thousand bolts of silk; Xun in Hunan fully memorialized this matter, saying Can communicated with military governors; Dezong was angry, and ordered Can's death; critics deemed it wrongful.

units.zh: 巽廉察江西，徇喜怒之情，而無罪被戮者多矣。
units.en: During his inspection tour in Jiangxi, Li Xun indulged his passions—and many innocent people were put to death.
units.literal: Xun as investigating commissioner in Jiangxi indulged feelings of favor and anger, and many who were guiltless were executed.

units.zh: 元和四年四月卒，時年七十一，贈尚書左僕射。
units.en: He died in the fourth month of 809, aged seventy-one, and was posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.
units.literal: Fourth month, fourth year of Yuanhe, he died, age seventy-one; posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

units.zh: 史臣曰：歷代操利柄為國計者，莫不損下益上，危人自安，變法以弄權，斂怨以構禍，皆有之矣。
units.en: The historian writes: Throughout history, those who held the reins of fiscal power in service of state finance have invariably enriched the throne at the people's expense, endangered others to save themselves, changed the laws to play politics, and stockpiled resentments that bred disaster—all of this has happened before.
units.literal: The historian says: In every age those who grasped the profit lever for state planning, without exception harmed the lower to benefit the upper, endangered others to secure themselves, changed laws to wield power, and gathered resentments to bring on calamity—all have had these.

units.zh: 如劉晏通擁滯，任才能，富其國而不勞於民，儉於家而利於眾。
units.en: Liu Yan was different: he cleared bottlenecks, put talent to use, enriched the state without overburdening the people, kept his household frugal, and brought benefit to all.
units.literal: Such as Liu Yan, who cleared congestion, employed talent and ability, enriched the state without burdening the people, was frugal in his household and beneficial to the multitude.

units.zh: 或問曰：鄭子產吏不能欺，宓子賤吏不忍欺，西門豹吏不敢欺。
units.en: One might ask: "With Zichan of Zheng, clerks could not cheat him; with Master Fu Ziqian, they could not bear to cheat him; with Ximen Bao, they did not dare cheat him."
units.literal: Someone asked: "Zi Chan of Zheng—clerks could not deceive him; Mi Zi Jian—clerks could not bear to deceive him; Xi Men Bao—clerks did not dare deceive him."

units.zh: 三子者，古之賢人也，吏皆懷其欺而不能、不忍、不敢也。
units.en: These three were sages of old. Their clerks may have wished to cheat them, but found themselves unable, unwilling, or too afraid.
units.literal: These three men were worthy men of antiquity; clerks all harbored deception but could not, could not bear to, and did not dare.

units.zh: 晏之吏，遠近自不欺者何也？
units.en: Why was it that Liu Yan's subordinates, near and far, simply did not cheat?
units.literal: Yan's clerks, near and far, naturally did not deceive—why?

units.zh: 答曰：蓋任其才而得其人也。
units.en: The answer: because he put the right people in the right roles and let them apply their talents.
units.literal: The answer: Probably because he employed their talents and obtained the right men.

units.zh: 晏歿，故吏二十余年繼掌財賦，不其是哉！
units.en: After Liu Yan's death, his former subordinates continued to manage the treasury for more than twenty years—is that not proof enough?
units.literal: When Yan died, his former clerks for more than twenty years successively managed finance and taxation—is this not proof!

units.zh: 《史記貨殖》云：「平糶齊物，關市不乏，治國之道也。」
units.en: The "Wealth and Profit" chapter of the Records of the Historian says, "Regulating grain prices to stabilize goods, keeping markets and frontier passes supplied—this is the art of governing."
units.literal: The "Wealth and Profit" chapter of the Records of the Historian says: "Evening out grain purchases to equalize goods, markets and passes not lacking—this is the way of governing a state."

units.zh: 晏治天下，無甚貴甚賤之物，泛言治國者，其可及乎！
units.en: Under Liu Yan's administration the realm saw neither ruinously high nor ruinously low prices. How many who speak of governing a nation can match that?
units.literal: Yan governed the realm; there were no extremely expensive or extremely cheap goods; speaking broadly of those who govern states, can they reach this!

units.zh: 舉真卿才，忠也，減王縉罪，正也，忠正之道，復出於人，嗚呼！
units.en: To recommend Yan Zhenqing showed loyalty; to lighten Wang Jin's punishment showed integrity. The virtues of loyalty and righteousness lived again in a single man—alas!
units.literal: Recommending Zhenqing's talent was loyalty; reducing Wang Jin's punishment was righteousness; the way of loyalty and righteousness again emerged in a person—alas!

units.zh: 本秀於林，風必摧之，常袞見忌於前，楊炎致冤於後，可為長嘆息矣！
units.en: A tree that stands above the forest is sure to be broken by the wind. Chang Gun resented him first; Yang Yan engineered his ruin afterward—enough to draw a long sigh.
units.literal: Timber outstanding in the forest—wind is sure to break it; Chang Gun envied him earlier; Yang Yan brought wrongful death later—one can only sigh long!

units.zh: 時譏有口者以利啖之，茍不塞讒口，何以持重權？
units.en: At the time, critics with wagging tongues were bought off with profit. Unless you silenced those tongues, how could you hold real power?
units.literal: At the time slanderers with mouths were fed with profit; if one does not stop slanderous mouths, how can one hold heavy power?

units.zh: 即無以展其才，濟其國矣。
units.en: Without that, there was no way to deploy one's abilities or serve the nation.
units.literal: Then there is no way to display one's talent and save the state.

units.zh: 是其術也，又何譏焉。
units.en: That was his approach—and what is there to condemn in it?
units.literal: This was his method—what is there to slander?

units.zh: 第五琦促辦應卒，民不加賦，而國豐饒，亦庶幾矣。
units.en: Fifth Qi mobilized resources swiftly in crisis without raising taxes on the people, and the treasury still grew flush—a feat nearly as admirable.
units.literal: Fifth Qi rushed preparations to meet emergencies; the people were not increased in taxes, yet the state was abundant—this too nearly succeeds.

units.zh: 然鑄錢變法，物貴身危，其何陋哉！
units.en: Yet his recoinage and legal tinkering drove up prices and put his own life at risk—how crude!
units.literal: Yet casting coins and changing laws made goods expensive and himself endangered—how base!

units.zh: 凡利國者，農商之外，不可為也。
units.en: As a rule, anything that enriches the state beyond agriculture and commerce should not be attempted.
units.literal: Generally what benefits the state—outside agriculture and commerce—cannot be done.

units.zh: 宏、滂爭權樹黨，皆非令人。
units.en: Ban Hong and Zhang Pang schemed for power and built factions—neither was a man one could respect.
units.literal: Hong and Pang fought for power and built factions—neither was a man to be admired.

units.zh: 紹之謹密幹事，巽之皦察精辨，亦足可稱。
units.en: Wang Shao's caution and efficiency, Li Xun's sharp-eyed precision—these too deserve recognition.
units.literal: Shao's discretion in handling affairs, Xun's clear scrutiny and precise discernment—also sufficient to praise.

units.zh: 贊曰：豐財忠良，晏道為長。
units.en: In praise: Enriching the treasury through loyal service—Liu Yan's way stands foremost.
units.literal: Eulogy: Abundant wealth and loyal integrity—Yan's way is foremost.

units.zh: 琦、宏、滂、巽，鹹以利彰。
units.en: Fifth Qi, Ban Hong, Zhang Pang, and Li Xun—all won fame through fiscal mastery.
units.literal: Qi, Hong, Pang, and Xun—all alike were famed through profit.

units.zh: 魏文侯時，西門豹為鄴令，有令名。
units.en: Under Marquis Wen of Wei, Ximen Bao governed Ye and earned an excellent reputation.
units.literal: In the time of Marquis Wen of Wei, Ximen Bao served as magistrate of Ye and had a good reputation.

units.zh: 至文侯曾孫襄王時，與群臣飲酒，王為群臣祝曰：「今吾臣皆西門豹之為人臣也！」
units.en: By the reign of King Xiang, Marquis Wen's great-grandson, the king drank with his court and toasted his ministers: "Would that all my ministers served as Ximen Bao did!"
units.literal: By the time of Marquis Wen's great-grandson King Xiang, while drinking with his ministers, the king toasted them, saying: "May all my ministers be like Ximen Bao in serving their ruler!"

units.zh: 漳水在其旁，西門豹不知用，是不智也。
units.en: The Zhang River lies right beside it, and Ximen Bao did not exploit it. That was not wisdom.
units.literal: The Zhang River is beside it; Ximen Bao did not know to use it - this is not wisdom.

units.zh: 仁智豹未之盡，何足法也！」
units.en: So Bao did not fully realize either wisdom or benevolence. Why should he be our standard?"
units.literal: Bao did not fully exhaust benevolence and wisdom; how can he be a sufficient model!"

units.zh: 硃泚反，李懷光又叛河中，使其將趙貴先築壘於同州，紓來奔奉天，向領州務。
units.en: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huaiguang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong prefecture; Li Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.
units.literal: Zhu Ci rebelled; Li Huaiguang also rebelled in Hezhong, sending his general Zhao Guixian to build fortifications at Tong Prefecture; Shu fled to Fengtian, and Xiang took charge of prefectural affairs.

units.zh: 李揆字端卿，隴西成紀人，而家於鄭州，代為冠族。
units.en: Li Kui, whose courtesy name was Duanqing, came from Longxi Chengji but his family had long lived in Zhengzhou, where for generations they ranked among the foremost great houses.
units.literal: Li Kui, styled Duanqing, was a native of Longxi Chengji but his family resided in Zhengzhou; for generations they were a leading clan.

units.zh: 揆嘗以主司取士，多不考實，徒峻其堤防，索其書策，殊未知藝不至者，文史之囿亦不能摛詞，深昧求賢之意也。
units.en: Kui had long felt that chief examiners, in selecting candidates, seldom tested real ability. They only raised barriers and demanded written answers, never recognizing that men without talent could not compose even within the familiar fields of letters and history. In this they utterly missed the purpose of seeking worthy men.
units.literal: Kui once observed that chief examiners in selecting scholars often did not verify true ability but merely heightened barriers and demanded written answers, wholly failing to see that those without talent could not compose even within the bounds of letters and histories—profoundly missing the intent of seeking the worthy.

units.zh: 開元末，舉進士，補陳留尉，獻書闕下，詔中書試文章，擢拜右拾遺。
units.en: Near the end of the Kaiyuan reign he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed defender of Chenliu. After he submitted a book to the court, the emperor ordered the Secretariat to examine his writings and promoted him to Right Remonstrance-reminder.
units.literal: At the end of the Kaiyuan era he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed Chenliu district defender, presented a memorial at the palace gates; on imperial order the Secretariat tested his literary compositions and he was promoted to Right Remonstrance-reminder.

units.zh: 改右補闕、起居郎，知宗子表疏。
units.en: He was then made Right Supplementation-reminder and Imperial Diarist, with responsibility for memorials from members of the imperial clan.
units.literal: He was transferred to Right Supplementation-reminder and Imperial Diarist, and was charged with imperial-clan memorials.

units.zh: 遷司勛員外郎、考功郎中，並知制誥。
units.en: He rose to outer office director of the Bureau of Merits and bureau director of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel, serving in both offices as a drafter of imperial rescripts.
units.literal: He was promoted to outer office director of the Bureau of Merits and bureau director of Evaluations in the Ministry of Personnel, and in both posts drafted imperial rescripts.

units.zh: 扈從劍南，拜中書舍人。
units.en: When the court went to Jiannan he accompanied it and was appointed a drafter of the Secretariat.
units.literal: He followed the emperor to Jiannan and was appointed Secretariat drafter.

units.zh: 乾元初，兼禮部侍郎。
units.en: Early in the Qianyuan era he was additionally appointed Vice Minister of Rites.
units.literal: At the beginning of the Qianyuan era he also served as Vice Minister of Rites.

units.zh: 由是數月之間，美聲上聞，未及畢事，遷中書侍郎、平章事、集賢殿崇文館大學士、修國史。
units.en: Within a few months his reputation for fairness reached the emperor. Before the examination cycle was even finished, he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, Grand Academician of the Jixian and Chongwen halls, and compiler of the national history.
units.literal: Within a few months his fine reputation reached the throne; before the examination was finished he was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, Grand Councilor, Grand Academician of the Jixian and Chongwen halls, and compiler of the national history.

units.zh: 自此頗承恩遇，遂蒙大用。
units.en: From that time he enjoyed marked imperial favor and was soon entrusted with great power.
units.literal: From then on he received considerable imperial favor and came to great employment.

units.zh: 少聰敏好學，善屬文。
units.en: As a youth he was quick-witted and devoted to study, and he excelled at literary composition.
units.literal: In youth he was clever and fond of learning, and skilled at literary composition.

units.zh: 其試進士文章，請於庭中設《五經》、諸史及《切韻》本於床，而引貢士謂之曰：「大國選士，但務得者，經籍在此，請恣尋檢。」
units.en: For the jinshi literary examination he had copies of the Five Classics, the standard histories, and the Qieyun placed on couches in the courtyard. He then brought the candidates before him and said, "A great state chooses its scholars only to find the able. The books are here—consult them freely."
units.literal: For the jinshi literary examination he requested that copies of the Five Classics, various histories, and the Qieyun be set on couches in the courtyard, and led the candidates in, saying: "A great state selects scholars only to obtain the able; the classics are here—please search and consult as you wish."

units.zh: 秦府學士、給事中玄道玄孫，秘書監、贈吏部尚書成裕之子。
units.en: He was the great-great-grandson of Xuandao, who had served as a scholar in the Prince of Qin's household and as a supervising remonstrator, and was the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat, who was posthumously made Minister of Personnel.
units.literal: He was the great-great-grandson of Xuandao, a scholar of the Prince of Qin's household and a supervising remonstrator; and the son of Chengyu, Director of the Secretariat and posthumously Minister of Personnel.

units.zh: 揆美風儀，善奏對，每有敷陳，皆符獻替。
units.en: Kui was distinguished in bearing and skilled in audience with the throne. Whatever he proposed was apt counsel, offered to improve and replace what was amiss.
units.literal: Kui had a fine bearing and was skilled in memorial replies; whenever he set forth proposals they accorded with the principle of offering and replacing.

units.zh: 肅宗賞嘆之，嘗謂揆曰：「卿門地、人物、文章，皆當代所推。」
units.en: Emperor Suzong admired him greatly and once told Kui, "Your family standing, your person, and your writings are all esteemed in our time."
units.literal: Emperor Suzong admired him and once said to Kui: "Your lineage, person, and writings are all praised in our age."

units.zh: 故進人稱為三絕。
units.en: For this reason contemporaries called him unmatched in three respects.
units.literal: Hence people at court called him the three incomparables.

units.zh: 其為舍人也，宗室請加張皇后「翊聖」之號，肅宗召揆問之，對曰；
units.en: While he served as a Secretariat drafter, members of the imperial clan petitioned to add the honorific "Assistant Sage" to Empress Zhang. Emperor Suzong summoned Kui for his view, and he answered:
units.literal: While he was a Secretariat drafter, members of the imperial clan asked to add the title "Assistant Sage" to Empress Zhang; Emperor Suzong summoned Kui and questioned him, and he replied:

units.zh: 「臣觀往古后妃，終則有謚。
units.en: "Your servant observes that in antiquity empresses and consorts received posthumous titles only after death.
units.literal: "Your servant observes that empresses and consorts of old received posthumous titles only at the end.

units.zh: 生加尊號，未之前聞。
units.en: To bestow a grand honorific title during one's lifetime is without precedent.
units.literal: To add an honorific title during life has never been heard of before.

units.zh: 景龍失政，韋氏專恣，加號翊聖，今若加皇后之號，與韋氏同。
units.en: In the Jinglong era the court lost its way, the Wei clan seized power, and the title Assistant Sage was added. If Your Majesty now adds such a title to the empress, you will be repeating the Wei precedent.
units.literal: In the Jinglong era government failed, the Wei clan acted willfully, and the title Assistant Sage was added; if Your Majesty now adds such a title to the empress, it will be the same as with the Wei.

units.zh: 陛下明聖，動遵典禮，豈可蹤景龍故事哉！」
units.en: Your Majesty is enlightened and always observant of ritual—how could you follow the Jinglong precedent!"
units.literal: Your Majesty is enlightened and sage and always follows the canonical rites—how could you follow the Jinglong precedent!"

units.zh: 肅宗驚曰：「凡才幾誤我家事。」
units.en: Emperor Suzong was startled and said, "Mediocre counsel nearly ruined my house."
units.literal: Emperor Suzong was startled and said: "Mediocre talent nearly ruined my household affairs."

units.zh: 遂止。
units.en: The proposal was then abandoned.
units.literal: The matter was then dropped.

units.zh: 揆因對見，肅宗從容曰：「成王嫡長有功，今當命嗣，卿意何如？」
units.en: On one audience Kui was present, and Emperor Suzong said calmly, "The Prince of Cheng is the eldest legitimate son and has rendered service. It is time to name the heir. What do you think?"
units.literal: When Kui came to audience, Emperor Suzong said calmly: "The Prince of Cheng is the eldest legitimate son and has merit; he should now be named heir—what is your view?"

units.zh: 揆拜賀曰：「陛下言及於此，社稷之福，天下幸甚，臣不勝大慶。」
units.en: Kui bowed in congratulation and said, "That Your Majesty speaks of this is a blessing to the altars of state and a great fortune for the realm. Your servant is overcome with joy."
units.literal: Kui bowed in congratulation and said: "That Your Majesty speaks of this is the fortune of the altars of soil and grain and great happiness for the realm; your servant cannot contain his great joy."

units.zh: 肅宗喜曰：「朕計決矣。」
units.en: Emperor Suzong said gladly, "My mind is made up."
units.literal: Emperor Suzong said with pleasure: "My decision is made."

units.zh: 時京師多盜賊，有通衢殺人置溝中者，李輔國方恣橫，上請選羽林騎士五百人以備巡檢。
units.en: At that time bandits were numerous in the capital; murders on busy streets and bodies thrown into ditches were common. Li Fuguo, then riding high in power, asked that five hundred Imperial Guard horsemen be chosen for patrol duty.
units.literal: At that time the capital had many bandits; some killed people on main roads and cast the bodies into ditches. Li Fuguo was then acting with unchecked arrogance and requested that five hundred Imperial Guard horsemen be selected for patrol inspection.

units.zh: 揆上疏曰：「昔西漢以南北軍相攝，故周勃因南軍入北軍，遂安劉氏。
units.en: Kui submitted a memorial saying, "In Western Han the Southern and Northern Armies were meant to check each other. That was why Zhou Bo, by way of the Southern Army, entered the Northern Army and thereby secured the Liu house.
units.literal: Kui submitted a memorial saying: "Formerly in Western Han the Southern and Northern Armies kept each other in check; therefore Zhou Bo entered the Northern Army through the Southern Army and thus secured the Liu house.

units.zh: 皇朝置南北衙，文武區分，以相伺察。
units.en: Our dynasty established the Northern and Southern Bureaus, separating civil and military authority so that each might watch the other.
units.literal: Our dynasty established the Northern and Southern Bureaus, separating civil and military, so that each might watch the other.

units.zh: 今以羽林代金吾警夜，忽有非常之變，將何以制之？」
units.en: If the Imperial Guard now replaces the Golden Crow in night patrol, and a sudden crisis arises, how will it be controlled?"
units.literal: Now to have the Imperial Guard replace the Golden Crow for night watch—if a sudden extraordinary change occurs, how will it be controlled?"

units.zh: 遂制罷羽林之請。
units.en: The request for Imperial Guard patrols was then ordered withdrawn.
units.literal: The request for Imperial Guard forces was then ordered withdrawn.

units.zh: 顏真卿為監察御史，使至隴右，翰嘗設宴，真卿謂翰曰：「中丞自郎將授將軍，便登節制，後生可畏，得無人乎？」
units.en: When Yan Zhenqing served as investigating censor and traveled to Longyou, Geshu Han once held a feast. Zhenqing said to him, "You rose from commandant to general and at once took a frontier command—there is much to fear in the young; surely you have capable men?"
units.literal: Yan Zhenqing was an investigating censor; when he was sent to Longyou, Han once gave a banquet, and Zhenqing said to Han, "Your Excellency went from commandant to general and straightway rose to a frontier command—youth can be feared; are there not men [among them]?"

units.zh: 顏真卿適自河北次於襄陽，謂仲犀曰：「曹使既果決，不顧萬死之地，何得沮之！
units.en: Yan Zhenqing, just arrived in Xiangyang from Hebei, told Zhongxi, "Commissioner Cao is so determined that he does not fear death itself—how can you hold him back?
units.literal: Yan Zhenqing happened to be stopping in Xiangyang on his way from Hebei and said to Zhongxi, "Commissioner Cao is so resolute that he does not shrink from a place of ten thousand deaths—how can you discourage him!

units.zh: 縱為賊所獲，是亡一使者；
units.en: Even if the rebels seized him, that would mean only one envoy lost;
units.literal: Even if he were taken by the rebels, that would be the loss of one envoy;

units.zh: 敬得入城，則萬人之心固矣。
units.en: but if he reaches the city, the hearts of ten thousand men will be secured.
units.literal: if he succeeds in entering the city, then the hearts of ten thousand men will be made firm.

units.zh: 公何愛焉？」
units.en: Why begrudge him the attempt?"
units.literal: Why do you begrudge him?"

units.zh: 轉運使劉晏奏令巡覆江西，多所蠲免。
units.en: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan had him tour and review Jiangxi, and many tax remissions were granted.
units.literal: Transport Commissioner Liu Yan memorialized to have him tour and review Jiangxi, and many remissions were granted.

units.zh: 佐晏征賦，頗有裨益，晏甚任之。
units.en: Assisting Yan in tax collection, he proved of considerable benefit, and Yan relied on him greatly.
units.literal: Assisting Yan in collecting taxes, he was of considerable benefit, and Yan greatly relied on him.

units.zh: 十一月，安祿山據范陽叛。
units.en: In the eleventh month An Lushan rebelled from Fanyang.
units.literal: In the eleventh month An Lushan seized Fanyang and rebelled.

units.zh: 十三日，祿山陷東京，常清以餘眾奔陜州，謂仙芝曰：「累日血戰，賊鋒不可當。
units.en: On the thirteenth Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his survivors to Shanzhou and told Xianzhi, "We have fought for days in blood — the rebel host cannot be stopped.
units.literal: On the thirteenth Lushan took the Eastern Capital; Changqing fled with his remaining troops to Shanzhou and said to Xianzhi: "For days we have fought in blood; the rebels' spearhead cannot be withstood.

units.zh: 宦官魚朝恩為觀軍容使，鎮陜州，與之昵狎。
units.en: The eunuch Yu Chao'en, army-observing commissioner at Shaanzhou, favored him.
units.literal: The eunuch Yu Chao'en was army-observing commissioner, garrisoned Shaanzhou, and was intimate with him.

units.zh: 朝恩以扈從功，恩渥崇厚，奏請多允，屢於上前賞拔智光，累遷華州刺史、同華二州節度使及潼關防禦使，加檢校工部尚書、兼御史大夫，
units.en: Chao'en's escort service won him favor; he praised Zhiguang again and again before the throne. Zhiguang rose to Governor of Hua, military governor of Tong and Hua, Tong Pass defender, and Acting Minister of Works with concurrent Censor-in-Chief.
units.literal: Chao'en for escort merit received thick favor; his requests were mostly granted; he repeatedly praised Zhiguang before the throne; Zhiguang was promoted repeatedly to Governor of Huazhou, military governor of Tong and Hua, defense commissioner of Tong Pass, and Acting Minister of Works with concurrent Censor-in-Chief,
